symptom: PC in VLAN 30 gets an IP but cannot reach another host in VLAN 30.
topology_note: PC-A on SW1 Fa0/1; both hosts should be VLAN 30.
show_outputs: show vlan brief: VLAN 30 missing; show interfaces Fa0/1 switchport: access VLAN 30.
evidence_summary: show vlan brief shows VLAN 30 is absent.
fix_steps: Create VLAN 30 and verify access-port assignment.

symptom: PC cannot communicate with a PC on the same subnet; port is up.
topology_note: PC connected to SW1 Fa0/5; intended VLAN is 20.
show_outputs: show interfaces Fa0/5 switchport: Access Mode VLAN 1.
expected_fault: Access port assigned to wrong VLAN.
evidence_summary: Fa0/5 is in VLAN 1 instead of VLAN 20.
fix_steps: Configure Fa0/5 as an access port in VLAN 20.

symptom: Multiple PCs in a remote VLAN lose connectivity after a switch link change.
topology_note: SW1-SW2 is intended to carry VLANs 10,20,30.
show_outputs: show interfaces trunk: allowed VLANs 10,20; VLAN 30 absent.
expected_fault: VLAN 30 missing from trunk allowed list.
evidence_summary: Trunk output excludes VLAN 30.
fix_steps: Allow VLAN 30 on the trunk and verify propagation.

symptom: Inter-switch communication fails for one VLAN only.
topology_note: SW1 G0/1 connects to SW2 G0/1.
show_outputs: show interfaces trunk: G0/1 trunking; native VLAN mismatch warning.
evidence_summary: Trunk status reports native VLAN mismatch.
fix_steps: Match native VLAN configuration on both trunk ends.

symptom: VLAN 20 hosts can communicate locally but cannot reach VLAN 30.
topology_note: Router-on-a-stick topology; R1 G0/0 connects to SW1 trunk.
show_outputs: show ip interface brief: G0/0.30 unconfigured.
evidence_summary: No G0/0.30 subinterface exists.
fix_steps: Create G0/0.30 with encapsulation dot1Q 30 and an IP gateway.

symptom: VLAN 20 host has correct IP but cannot ping its default gateway.
topology_note: Gateway should be 192.168.20.1.
show_outputs: show ip interface brief: G0/0.20 192.168.30.1 up/up.
expected_fault: Gateway subinterface has wrong IP network.
evidence_summary: Subinterface G0/0.20 uses 192.168.30.1 instead of 192.168.20.1.
fix_steps: Assign the correct VLAN 20 gateway address.

symptom: Hosts in VLAN 10 can reach gateway but not VLAN 20.
topology_note: R1 routes VLANs using subinterfaces.
show_outputs: show run interface G0/0.20: encapsulation dot1Q 10.
expected_fault: VLAN 20 subinterface uses wrong VLAN tag.
evidence_summary: G0/0.20 is tagged for VLAN 10.
fix_steps: Change encapsulation to dot1Q 20 and verify.

symptom: PC can reach its gateway but not a remote server network.
topology_note: R1 should reach 10.10.40.0/24 through 10.10.30.2.
show_outputs: show ip route: no 10.10.40.0/24 entry.
evidence_summary: Routing table has no route for 10.10.40.0/24.
fix_steps: Add the correct static route or restore the routing protocol.

symptom: Remote network is reachable from router but not from PC.
topology_note: PC subnet is 192.168.10.0/24; R1 has route to 10.10.40.0/24.
show_outputs: show ip route: route present; PC default gateway is 192.168.10.254; R1 LAN IP is 192.168.10.1.
evidence_summary: PC gateway does not match the router LAN address.
fix_steps: Set PC default gateway to 192.168.10.1.

symptom: Router has a route but traffic still fails to return to source network.
topology_note: Two-router topology with remote LANs.
show_outputs: show ip route 192.168.10.0: network not found on R2.
evidence_summary: R2 lacks a route back to 192.168.10.0/24.
fix_steps: Add a return route or correct dynamic routing.

symptom: Routing protocol neighbors are not forming.
topology_note: R1 and R2 are directly connected.
show_outputs: show ip protocols: OSPF process active; show ip interface brief: link up/up; show run: different area IDs.
evidence_summary: Interfaces are up but OSPF area configuration differs.
fix_steps: Configure matching OSPF area settings.

symptom: A directly connected server cannot be reached from router.
topology_note: Server network should be 172.16.50.0/24.
show_outputs: show ip interface brief: G0/1 administratively down.
evidence_summary: G0/1 is administratively down.
fix_steps: Enable G0/1 and verify link/IP configuration.

symptom: PC receives 169.254.x.x address instead of a lab subnet address.
topology_note: DHCP server is on another subnet.
show_outputs: ipconfig: 169.254.10.5; show run interface G0/0.20: no ip helper-address.
evidence_summary: No helper address exists on the client VLAN interface.
fix_steps: Add the DHCP server IP with ip helper-address.

symptom: PC receives an IP address but cannot use the intended gateway.
topology_note: DHCP pool should serve 192.168.20.0/24.
show_outputs: show run | section dhcp: default-router 192.168.30.1.
evidence_summary: DHCP pool advertises a gateway from another subnet.
fix_steps: Correct the default-router value and renew the lease.

symptom: New clients cannot obtain addresses while existing clients work.
topology_note: DHCP pool is for 192.168.10.0/24.
show_outputs: show ip dhcp pool: 100% utilization.
evidence_summary: Pool utilization is 100%.
fix_steps: Expand the address pool or release unused leases.

symptom: Only clients on one VLAN fail to get DHCP addresses.
topology_note: Server works for VLAN 10; VLAN 20 fails.
show_outputs: show run interface G0/0.20: ip helper-address points to 192.168.99.99; actual server is 192.168.99.10.
evidence_summary: Helper address does not match the DHCP server IP.
fix_steps: Correct the helper address.

symptom: PC can ping server IP but cannot open server by hostname.
topology_note: DNS server is 192.168.50.10.
show_outputs: ipconfig /all: DNS server 192.168.50.99; ping 192.168.50.10 succeeds.
expected_fault: Wrong DNS server configured on client.
evidence_summary: Client points to 192.168.50.99 instead of the DNS server.
fix_steps: Configure the correct DNS server and retry name resolution.

symptom: Hostname resolution fails but direct IP access works.
topology_note: DNS service should run on Server1.
show_outputs: Server DNS service: Off.
evidence_summary: Server shows DNS service disabled.
fix_steps: Enable DNS service and verify the record.

symptom: One website name fails while other names resolve.
topology_note: DNS server is reachable.
show_outputs: DNS table has no A record for intranet.local.
evidence_summary: Expected hostname has no corresponding DNS record.
fix_steps: Add the correct A record and test resolution.

symptom: PC can reach gateway but cannot reach server on TCP 80.
topology_note: ACL is applied inbound on router LAN interface.
show_outputs: show access-lists: deny tcp 192.168.10.0 0.0.0.255 host 10.10.40.10 eq 80.
evidence_summary: ACL contains a deny statement matching source, destination, and port.
fix_steps: Modify/remove the blocking rule according to policy.

symptom: Ping works but SSH to router fails from management subnet.
topology_note: Management access should permit SSH.
show_outputs: show access-lists: deny tcp 192.168.20.0 0.0.0.255 any eq 22.
evidence_summary: ACL denies TCP port 22 from management subnet.
fix_steps: Add an appropriate permit for authorized management hosts.

symptom: Guest VLAN can access an internal server that should be isolated.
topology_note: Guest subnet is 192.168.50.0/24; server is 10.10.40.10.
show_outputs: show access-lists: no deny from 192.168.50.0/24 to 10.10.40.0/24.
evidence_summary: ACL has no rule denying guest-to-internal traffic.
fix_steps: Add a policy-compliant deny for guest access to internal networks.

symptom: Inside PC can reach router but cannot reach Internet address.
topology_note: PAT should translate 192.168.10.0/24.
show_outputs: show ip nat translations: empty; show run: no ip nat inside source command.
evidence_summary: No translations and no NAT source rule are present.
fix_steps: Configure PAT using the correct inside interface/access list.

symptom: NAT is configured but translations are not created.
topology_note: R1 has inside LAN and outside WAN interfaces.
show_outputs: show run interface G0/0: ip nat inside; G0/1: no ip nat outside.
evidence_summary: WAN interface is not marked ip nat outside.
fix_steps: Configure ip nat outside on the WAN interface.

symptom: Only some inside hosts reach the Internet.
topology_note: NAT ACL should include 192.168.10.0/24.
show_outputs: show access-lists NAT_ACL: permit 192.168.20.0 0.0.0.255.
evidence_summary: NAT ACL permits 192.168.20.0/24, not the actual client subnet.
fix_steps: Correct the NAT ACL network and verify translations.

symptom: Laptop associates with SSID but receives no usable IP.
topology_note: AP connects clients to VLAN 30.
show_outputs: Laptop IP: 169.254.2.3; DHCP pool for VLAN 30 exists; AP uplink is access VLAN 1.
evidence_summary: AP uplink is placed in VLAN 1 instead of the wireless client VLAN.
fix_steps: Correct AP uplink VLAN configuration.

symptom: Clients can connect to Wi-Fi but cannot reach internal resources.
topology_note: Guest SSID should be isolated.
show_outputs: SSID mapped to internal VLAN 10 instead of guest VLAN 50.
evidence_summary: SSID is mapped to an internal VLAN.
fix_steps: Map the SSID to the intended guest VLAN and apply isolation policy.

symptom: Wireless client frequently disconnects while wired clients are stable.
topology_note: AP channel overlaps with nearby AP in lab simulation.
show_outputs: Wireless settings show same channel and interference warning.
evidence_summary: Wireless configuration indicates channel overlap/interference.
fix_steps: Choose a non-overlapping channel and retest.

symptom: Laptop connects to SSID but authentication fails.
topology_note: WPA2 key should match AP configuration.
show_outputs: Client security key differs from AP configured key.
evidence_summary: Client and AP security credentials do not match.
fix_steps: Use the correct authorized security configuration.

symptom: PC suddenly loses connectivity after a switch-port change.
topology_note: Port should be enabled and connected to the client VLAN.
show_outputs: show interfaces Fa0/10 status: err-disabled.
evidence_summary: Port status explicitly shows err-disabled.
fix_steps: Identify the cause, correct the configuration, then safely recover the port.
